svg.text: OnCall Copilot for Slack — what is built, what is not, and why
Product & delivery status map · codebase v0.37.0 · workbook v037 · tracker v030
MoPr08 · prepared for Senthil / KP · 20 September 2026 · sources: Perplexity independent review V001, ChatGPT external review V001, audit.mjs v3
Built, tested, and a user could reach it today
Built and proven — cannot reach the real platform yet
Some of it exists; the rest is a scheduled sprint
1 · How one incident flows through the product today

The spine is complete and proven. The three amber steps are the only reason an engineer cannot finish an incident yet: the adapters that call Slack, the pager and the status page are not written — everything they plug into is.
The only surface the product needs — Slack

deploy or a kill -9 cannot lose it.

Why the last three steps are amber, not red

Every contract those adapters must satisfy is finished: asynchronous, budgeted (a hung call degrades instead of hanging), health-probed at boot, and refused by name in production so a stub can never ship by accident. Writing them is plumbing against a live workspace —
30 minutes of your time (SC-06) unblocks the largest single item in the plan.
2 · Layer by layer — what is done, what is not, and the reason
Nine layers make up the product. Five are finished and proven by 616 tests at 100% coverage over both src/ and scripts/. The rest are blocked on something specific and named.
Declare, mitigate, resolve, reopen with illegal transitions refused; first
resolution immutable so MTTR cannot drift; automatic timeline; blameless postmortem
One workflow per workspace (no cross-tenant reads); role matrix; audit log; plan
limits actually enforced on the write path; export/delete covering all seven tenant
Nine Postgres stores, 14 ordered migrations, atomic ids and usage claims, leased
jobs that run once per interval, a deferred queue that survives kill -9 — all
verified against a real PostgreSQL 16 in CI.
Production refuses to start on a stub, an in-memory store, or an adapter that fails
its healthcheck — and is proven to permit a healthy one. The closed provider set
616 tests / 100% statements, branches, functions, lines over src AND scripts;
adversarial suite; real-Postgres job; load run; audit.mjs v3 which found a defect
The declare modal, the incident message with Mitigate/Resolve/Reopen, and App Home
are all built and validated against Slack's Block Kit limits — but nothing renders
them until views.open and chat.postMessage exist (S38).
Slack Web API, OAuth exchange, response_url poster, views.open,
PagerDuty/JSM/Compass/webhook, AI provider, status vendor, Stripe. Contracts,
honest stubs and the gate that refuses them exist; the HTTP calls do not. S38 · S40
No SAML/OIDC, no SCIM, no Enterprise Grid model, no managed KMS, no SBOM or image
signing, no third-party penetration test, no SOC 2 process. The enterprise-ready
claim is formally withdrawn (gate G0). S43 · S44 · S48.
Latency measured in-process and gating CI, operator webhook alerts, blue/green
workflow and a backup drill scripted. Missing: structured logs, OTel traces, SLOs,
chaos and restore drills, listing assets, design partners, pricing validation. S42
3 · What is pending, in the order it must happen, and what unblocks it
The review's central instruction was a sequence, not a defect: convert the boundary before wiring adapters. Phase 0 (PX-S0/S1/S2) is done, so the queue below is now genuinely in order.
S37 · Durable data plane, proven under
Kill one replica mid-declare; assert no lost or
A deploy topology (2 replicas + real Postgres)
SC-06: a Slack dev workspace + signing secret
read-only, invoices, proration on band changes.
Importer, mapping report, dry run, landing page —
D-OC7 ratification + a sample Opsgenie export
PagerDuty Events v2, JSM, Compass, generic
webhook behind the widened provider type.
Vendor accounts; PX-S3 first by choice
Able to run in parallel once the spine lands

S42 SRE, observability, HA & DR (also closes PX-014/PX-015) · S43 KMS, SAML/OIDC, SCIM, SBOM, licence · S44 Enterprise Grid · S45 AI incident intelligence — the real differentiator · S46 integrations · S47 Slack UX & activation · S48 compliance & procurement pack
15 interviews, 5 partners, price tests on the banded model. The computed plan needs 305
paying workspaces and about $215k of runway — no customer has seen a price yet.
D13 is parked portfolio-wide; needs unparking. Calendar time, not code — can start today.
Third-party penetration test, a THIRD independent review, live Slack + Stripe sweep,
load/soak on real infrastructure, manual accessibility pass.
A pen-test vendor and a reviewer independent of both previous ones. No self-signoff.
Listing, migration landing page, comparison pages, case studies, two enterprise pilots,
Slack's manual review queue cannot be accelerated and re-triggers on any listing change.

The one-line summary: the engine is finished and proven; the wires to Slack, the pager, Stripe and the status page are not. Nothing after PX-S2 was started before PX-S2 closed, which is why S38 is now plumbing rather than redesign.
Not completed ≠ not attempted. Every amber and grey box above is blocked on a named credential, vendor, decision or piece of infrastructure — not on engineering time.
